items.title: 52222_Marshall Royal oral history interview
items.q: By me doing that, we became very, very close friends, Billie and I, and it lasted throughout her lifetime.

ctx.x: Well, we came into the Sherman Hotel around, I believe it was 1941. We were one of the first of a group of jazz artists that performed at the Panther Room and that was a room that they served the food on the flaming swords and such things as that, quite an elegant room. So, Lionel Hampton was the featured performer there with his orchestra and he had a supporting act there by the name of Billie Holliday. So, before we -- after we had rehearsals and right before we went into our beginning show that night, Lionel…

So, since I was standing up in front of the band and I announced her and brought her on the floor and I was the one that was leading the applause when she finished, I thought it no more than right that I should bring her back as many times as she warranted. Since Miss Billie Holliday was one of a kind in her particular type of singing, she warranted several encores, which I proceeded to give to her, for which I was roundly chewed out when I finished the night's performance by my band leader, Mr. Hampton.
